newsitem.title: FRANCE: Chirac unconvincing about policies -- poll.
newsitem.headline: Chirac unconvincing about policies -- poll.

text.p: President Jacques Chirac was unconvincing in a television interview this week when he said France should stick with austerity policies and ruled out a cabinet reshuffle, an opinion poll showed on Saturday.

The survey, by Ipsos Opinion for the Journal du Dimanche newspaper and France 2 television, showed that 58 percent of citizens rated Chirac unconvincing in his television appearance on Thursday, against 29 percent who rated him convincing.

It was the second blow to conservative Chirac's hopes of lifting gloom in France with his first extended interview since July -- a survey by the daily Liberation released on Friday evening showed similar conclusions.

Chirac pledged to stick to tight fiscal policies needed to help France qualify for a single European currency from 1999. And he said Prime Minister Alain Juppe's government was on the right track to revive the economy and cut record unemployment.

The Ipsos survey, of 965 people on December 13 and 14, showed those polled rated Chirac most convincing in talking about fighting terrorism and least convincing in discussing ways of cutting youth unemployment.
Fifty-three percent of those polled said they had seen the interview -- others had seen excerpts, read or heard about it.
